claims.text: The modified material is an equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy.
WTaTiVZr has superior plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
The proposed superiority of WTaTiVZr arises from altered dislocation dynamics.
The multi-principal-element composition introduces local lattice distortions and heterogeneous chemical ordering.
Local lattice distortions and chemical heterogeneity transform the dominant deformation mode from screw-dislocation-dominated slip to edge-dislocation and heterogeneous slip.
Pure tungsten exhibits brittle, predominantly screw-dislocation-dominated behavior under the stated conditions.
Structural variations in WTaTiVZr modify the dislocation-core energy landscape.
The modified dislocation energy landscape favors mobile edge dislocations and heterogeneous slip systems over screw-dislocation motion.
Heterogeneous dislocation pathways can permit substantial plastic deformation while maintaining strength and strain hardening.
Crack bridging can inhibit fracture by shielding a crack from the applied driving force.
The altered slip mode in WTaTiVZr enables nanoscale crack bridging.
Crack-tip bridging and distributed plasticity delay crack initiation and propagation in WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr is expected to exhibit a higher density of mobile edge dislocations than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr is expected to form distinctive heterogeneous slip bands.
WTaTiVZr is expected to show nanoscale crack bridging, delayed cracking, and greater ductility and toughness than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, pure tungsten will initiate cracks earlier and show no significant crack bridging.
The proposed behavior applies at approximately 800–1200 °C and may not occur outside that range or outside the controlled strain-rate regime.
The stated temperature and strain-rate conditions are representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
Identically loaded in situ tests of WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten can compare dislocation character, slip localization, crack evolution, plastic strain, and toughness.
